title: One Seed, Many Streams: Randomness That Does Not Change When You Add a Sensor

questions.question: Why does adding a logging camera to a simulation sometimes change a bug that has nothing to do with it?
options: All the parts draw from one generator, so each part's numbers depend on how many draws the others made: with the camera added the imu's noise changed in 1000 of 1000 values
questions.explanation: The imu was given the camera's numbers.

questions.question: What is the avalanche property of a mixer?
options: Changing one bit of the input changes about half the output bits: 32.1 of 64 on average here, so neighbouring seeds look unrelated
questions.explanation: A mixer that flipped few bits would give seeds 1 and 2 similar streams.

questions.question: How is a part's seed made?
options: From its index in a list
From the master seed and a hash of the part's name, so it does not depend on which other parts exist or the order they were made in
questions.explanation: The same master and name always give the same seed.

questions.question: What does a seed of zero do to a xorshift generator, and to this stream?
options: A xorshift generator stays at zero; this stream's successive numbers differ, since it adds a constant before mixing
questions.explanation: The state is advanced by a large odd number first.

questions.question: Streams for the encoder and the imu were asked for in opposite orders in two simulations. What happened?
options: The motor's and the imu's numbers were identical in both: the order of first asking changes nothing
questions.explanation: Each is made from its name.
